newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Gold - Producers, RBA, stay out of market.
newsitem.headline: Australia Gold - Producers, RBA, stay out of market.

text.p: Australian gold producers have not joined South Africa's Western Areas mining complex in buying back gold hedges because of a prevailing view here that the gold price will continue to head down.
Bullion dealers say many Australian gold miners are believed to be considering buying back gold in hedging programmes.

"(But) it's a matter of being confident you're at somewhere near the lows and I suspect that a lot of people are holding off because they're not confident we've seen the worst yet," Mark Fremantle of Rothschild Australia Ltd said.
Other bullion dealers contacted by Reuters echoed the same view.
Another recent Australian player in the world gold market is also keeping a low profile.

The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), which triggered the metal's recent price collapse to a 12-year low of about US$314 an ounce in early July after it announced it had sold 167 tonnes of gold over the past six months, said on Thursday it was not among central banks rumoured to be sellers.
An RBA spokesman said earlier statements by the bank that it would not be selling more gold could be taken as "gospel".

Confirmation that Australian gold producers had not begun to buy back gold and that the RBA had not sold more of the metal followed gold's weakness on Wednesday on fresh rumours of central bank gold sales and conclusion of the gold hedge buy-back by Western Areas mines.
This knocked the gold price back to $321.40/90 at midday Thursday in Hong Kong from the opening of $322.60/323.10.
"I'd heard a rumour (of central bank sales), but as to names, and who and where and why, nothing," Macquarie Bank dealer John Israel said.
Rothschild's Fremantle said further sales by central banks "could be the case but today they've been holding off".
Rothschilds had not seen central bank gold activity below the $340-$350 area, he said.
"And they certainly have a different timeframe to most market participants. I expect that most of them would be quite patient even if they do want to sell," he said.
Australian bullion dealers agree also that the gold market faces further tests, with most see it continuing to slide to test the recent low at $314 an ounce.
With the Western Areas buy-back out of the way, the market was seen drifting lower and likely to test $314 in the near future, Israel said.
Fremantle also saw a reasonable chance gold will test $314, possibly trading sideways toward that level and vulnerable to bad news.
Another analyst sees gold likely to fall further, possibly to about $310 an oz, although predictions of a gold price of less than $300 were the sweepings of sentiment, he said.
"If it can keep its head above water at $320 ... I'm not as bearish as other people around," he said. Gold's fundamentals were still sound, he said.

"It was just more a shock that the Australian Reserve Bank, of all people ... it wasn't so much the amount of gold, which was a pittance, but it just knocks people's confdence around. The outlook is not too bad and hopefully it will stabilise and work its way back up slowly," he said.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
